tool.name: BARS blinded review
tool.description: de-identify manuscripts and score them with Gemini against the BARS rubric
tool.command: #if $source.source_type == 'ids_file' ## one manifest row per identifier line: tabs/CRs flattened, blank and comment lines skipped tr '\t\r' ' ' < '$source.ids_file' | awk 'NF && \$1 !~ /^#/ { print "id\t" \$0 "\t" }' > manifest.tsv && #else cp '$manifest' manifest.tsv && #end if PYTHONPATH='${__tool_directory__}' python -m bars run --manifest manifest.tsv --outdir out --mode '$mode' --model '@MODEL@' --max-papers @MAX_PAPERS@ #if $redact_terms --redact-terms '$terms_file' #end if #if $source.source_type == 'upload' $source.confirm_not_confidential #end if

configfiles.configfile: #set $TAB = chr(9) #if $source.source_type == 'ids_text' #for $line in str($source.ids).splitlines() #set $value = ' '.join($line.split()) #if $value and not $value.startswith('#') id${TAB}${value}${TAB} #end if #end for #elif $source.source_type == 'upload' #for $manuscript in $source.manuscripts #set $kind = 'pdf' if $manuscript.ext == 'pdf' else 'jats' #set $label = ' '.join(str($manuscript.element_identifier).split()) ${kind}${TAB}${manuscript}${TAB}${label} #end for #end if

tool.help:
.. class:: warningmark
**Do not upload manuscripts you received for confidential peer review.** In review mode the de-identified text is sent to a third-party API (Google Gemini). Upload only your own manuscripts or published papers.
-----
**What it does**
BARS (Blinded AI Review System) writes a structured, blinded peer review of each manuscript and scores it with the BARS rubric (``REVIEW_TEMPLATE.md`` v1.1 from https://github.com/spond/gemini-reviews). For every manuscript the tool:
1. **Ingests** the full text: fetched by identifier from Europe PMC (open-access JATS XML only) or uploaded (JATS XML or PDF). 2. **De-identifies** it. The title, authors, affiliations, correspondence, journal, publication year, DOI, PMID and PMCID are never emitted; acknowledgements, funding, author contributions, competing interests and the reference list are dropped. In the remaining text e-mail addresses, ORCIDs, author names (including "Surname et al." citations), institutions, e-mail domains, journal names, years after publication and your extra terms are replaced by typed placeholders such as ``[AUTHOR_REDACTED]`` or ``[INSTITUTION_REDACTED]``. Links are replaced by typed placeholders (``[CODE_REPO_URL]``, ``[GALAXY_HISTORY_URL]``, ``[GALAXY_WORKFLOW_URL]``, ``[WORKFLOW_REGISTRY_URL]``, ``[DATA_ARCHIVE_URL]``, ``[DATA_ARCHIVE_DOI]``, ``[PUBLIC_DATABASE_URL]``, ``[DOI_REDACTED]``, ``[URL_REDACTED]``) so the reviewer still knows that code and data were linked. Data and code availability statements are kept; accession numbers are kept. 3. **Leak-checks** the scrubbed text and fails closed: if any blocking identifier remains (e-mail, ORCID, URL, DOI, author name, institution, journal, extra term ...) the manuscript is *not* sent to the reviewer (status ``leak_blocked``). Weaker signals are reported as warnings. 4. **Reviews** it (review mode only): the scrubbed text, under an anonymous ID such as ``MANUSCRIPT_001``, is sent with the BARS template as system instruction to the Gemini API (model ``@MODEL@``, temperature 1.0, no web search or URL tools). 5. **Parses** the scores (Rigor /3.5, Claims /2.5, Biology /2.0, Reproducibility /2.0, Total /10, Scientific Core /8 and tier) and checks that they are in range, add up and match the tier.
Bibliographic metadata is re-attached to each review (provenance footer) only after the review text is final.
-----
**Inputs**
- **Identifiers**, typed in or as a text dataset: PMCID (``PMC9629619``), PMID (``PMID:36322727`` or bare digits) or DOI (``10.1371/journal.pone.0123456``, ``doi:...``, ``https://doi.org/...``). Only open-access articles with full text in Europe PMC can be fetched; others get status ``not_open_access`` or ``fetch_error``. - **Uploads**: JATS XML (best) or PDF. PDF de-identification is heuristic (author names are guessed from the front matter), so check the scrubbed text and leak report. A PDF in which no author names are found is not sent for review (status ``leak_blocked``, leak kind ``no_authors``) unless you list its authors under *Extra terms to redact*. Uploads require the confidentiality confirmation. - **Mode**: *review* runs the full pipeline; *scrub* stops after de-identification and the leak check and makes no API call (identifier inputs still contact Europe PMC). Use scrub mode to inspect exactly what would be sent. - **Extra terms to redact**: names or phrases the automatic rules cannot know about (lab nicknames, cohort or project names). They are used exactly as typed, in any script; straight and curly apostrophes match each other.
At most @MAX_PAPERS@ manuscripts per job. Manuscripts are processed one after another; a failure in one does not stop the others.
-----
**Outputs**
- **scores** (tabular, one row per manuscript): ``id, name, input_type, status, total, core, rigor, claims, biology, reproducibility, tier, score_source, score_issues, leaks_block, leaks_warn, model, model_version, prompt_tokens, output_tokens, thinking_tokens, seconds, message``. ``status`` is one of ``ok``, ``scores_invalid`` (review written but scores missing or inconsistent, see ``score_issues``), ``scrubbed`` (scrub mode), ``not_open_access``, ``fetch_error``, ``ingest_error``, ``leak_blocked`` or ``review_error``. - **leak report** (tabular): every remaining identifier found by the leak check (``id, name, kind, severity, match, context``); ``block`` rows prevented the review. - **run metadata** (json): tool and template versions, model, settings, timestamps and per-manuscript redaction counts and dropped sections. - **scrubbed manuscripts** (collection of markdown): exactly the text the reviewer sees (or would see). - **reviews** (collection of markdown, review mode only): the reviewer's report with a provenance footer.
The job fails with exit code 1 when no manuscript could be processed, and with exit code 2 for an invalid request (no or too many inputs, uploads without confirmation, no API key configured).
-----
**Data handling and the API key**
In review mode the de-identified text is sent to Google's Gemini API on the paid tier, under which Google does not use prompts or responses to train its models. Users do not enter a key: the Galaxy server administrators supply it as the environment variable ``BARS_GEMINI_API_KEY``, and it is visible to them in job scripts. Ask your administrators whether this tool is enabled with a key on your server.
-----
**Limitations**
- Scores are **uncalibrated** relative to the published BARS study: that study ran Gemini through Antigravity subagents, while this tool calls the API directly, so scores are not directly comparable to the BARS leaderboard or calibration tables. - The reviewer sees **text only**: figure images, supplementary files and code are not provided (figure legends and tables are included as text). - Reviews are stochastic; repeated runs on the same manuscript differ. In testing, four runs of one manuscript gave totals from 6.8 to 7.4, enough to change the tier. Treat differences of less than about one point as noise. - De-identification is automated and can miss identifiers or remove harmless words; check the scrubbed text and leak report. - At most @MAX_PAPERS@ manuscripts per job (running the tool over a collection starts one job per element).
